problem: Mixture-of-Experts models require retaining all experts in memory during deployment, incurring substantial memory overhead that limits practical scalability.
approach: MoNE replaces low-usage, low-variance experts with lightweight neural estimators called novices that approximate their outputs, factorizing expert redundancy by access frequency and output variance metrics.
contribution: Outperforms baselines by up to 2.72 average zero-shot accuracy across nine tasks at 25% pruning ratio with only 0.14 performance drop on Qwen2-57B-A14B.

problem: Safety alignment in LLMs degrades during fine-tuning even on benign data or with parameter-efficient methods, leading to harmful model behavior.
approach: GuardSpace decomposes pre-trained weights into safety-relevant and safety-irrelevant components via SVD, freezing safety components and constraining adapter updates to a null space that preserves safe outputs on harmful prompts.
contribution: Reduces average harmful score from 14.4% to 3.6% on Llama-2-7B-Chat for GSM8K while improving accuracy from 26.0% to 28.0%.

problem: LLM robustness in extended multi-turn conversations remains poorly understood; existing benchmarks focus on static single-turn assessments that miss real-world temporal degradation patterns.
approach: Applies survival analysis models (Cox proportional hazards, Accelerated Failure Time, Random Survival Forest) to 36,951 dialogue turns to model conversational failure as a time-to-event process with semantic drift features.
contribution: Establishes survival analysis as a paradigm for evaluating multi-turn robustness; turn-level risk monitors flag failing conversations several turns before the first inconsistency while maintaining modest false-alert rates.

problem: Vision-language navigation for UAVs is limited to instruction-following in known environments; real-world autonomous exploration requires navigating unknown terrain with only coarse positional guidance and continuous obstacle avoidance.
approach: AutoFly is an end-to-end Vision-Language-Action model combining pseudo-depth encoding for spatial reasoning with progressive two-stage training to align visual, depth, and linguistic representations with action policies.
contribution: Constructed a novel autonomous navigation dataset emphasizing continuous planning and obstacle avoidance; AutoFly achieves robust autonomous UAV navigation in real-world scenarios without detailed pre-specified instructions.

problem: Visual stimulus reconstruction from fMRI signals depends critically on identifying the correct latent space structure and generative model that align with neural encoding, but this remains unclear.
approach: PRISM projects fMRI signals into a structured text space via language model embeddings, using object-centric diffusion to compose individual objects and an attribute-relationship search module to align with neural activity patterns.
contribution: Demonstrates that text space better captures fMRI signals than vision or joint spaces; object-centric composition reduces detection errors in visual stimulus reconstruction from brain activity.

problem: Scalable evaluation during training and inference requires specialized generative evaluators, but recent methods focus on new algorithmic approaches rather than data-driven development at scale.
approach: FARE trains 8B and 20B parameter evaluators on 2.5M curated samples across five evaluation tasks (pairwise, step-level, verification, rating) via iterative rejection-sampling supervised fine-tuning.
contribution: FARE-20B sets the new standard for open-source evaluators, surpassing specialized 70B+ models; as verifiers in RL training, FARE improves downstream model performance by up to 14.1% versus string-matching baselines.

problem: Verifiable rewards for LLM reasoning provide only coarse-grained correctness feedback, leading to inefficient reasoning with verbose or repetitive outputs; length penalties compromise accuracy.
approach: Self-Aligned Reward (SAR) measures relative perplexity difference between answer conditioned on query and standalone answer, favoring concise, query-specific responses and complementing verifiable rewards in RL.
contribution: Across 4 models and 7 benchmarks, integrating SAR with PPO and GRPO reduces answer length by 30% while improving accuracy by 4%; achieves Pareto-optimal frontier between correctness and efficiency.

problem: Exact Gaussian processes on graphs have O(N^3) time complexity, prohibiting Bayesian inference on large discrete input spaces; scalable approximations are needed.
approach: Applies graph random features (GRFs) as stochastic estimators of graph node kernels to enable O(N^{3/2}) scalable Gaussian process inference with probabilistic accuracy guarantees.
contribution: Enables Bayesian optimization on over 1M graph nodes on a single computer with wall-clock speedups and memory savings while preserving competitive performance.

problem: Universal Test-Time Adaptation under dual class and domain shifts relies on heuristic approaches and struggles with significant shifts; adaptation imbalance from limited annotations hampers performance.
approach: EMAC incorporates active human annotation into test-time adaptation by identifying mixed regions under dual shifts, using reward-guided selection to prioritize representative samples, and balancing pseudo-labels with limited annotations.
contribution: Active Universal Test-Time Adaptation significantly improves performance and achieves state-of-the-art results by strategically annotating high-uncertainty regions.
theme: Transfer Learning, Meta Learning & Lifelong Learning

problem: Text-to-image diffusion models struggle to reconcile multiple spatial conditions; existing approaches require costly retraining or labor-intensive manual weight tuning.
approach: Cross-ControlNet fuses features from multiple ControlNet branches using pixel-wise fusion guided by smoothed variance maps, channel-wise hybrid fusion via consistency gates, and key-value injection for disentangling conflicting conditions.
contribution: Training-free framework achieves consistent improvements in controllable generation under both conflicting and complementary conditions and generalizes to DiT-based FLUX models without additional training.

problem: Financial agents require complex multi-step searches over time-sensitive, domain-specific data; existing benchmarks lack realistic financial tasks that reflect analyst workflows and require deep expertise to construct.
approach: FinSearchComp comprises three realistic tasks (Time-Sensitive Data Fetching, Simple Historical Lookup, Complex Historical Investigation) with 635 expert-annotated questions validated by 70 professional financial experts across global and Greater China markets.
contribution: First open-source financial agent benchmark; Grok 4 approaches expert-level accuracy on global markets; web search and financial plugins significantly improve agent performance.

problem: Audio-Visual Question Answering treats audio as complementary to video and integrates question information only late, underutilizing frequency-domain audio characteristics and query-guided reasoning.
approach: QSTar incorporates question-guided clues and exploits frequency-domain audio analysis alongside spatial-temporal perception; Query Context Reasoning block prompts models to focus on semantically relevant audio-visual features.
contribution: Significant performance improvements over Audio QA, Visual QA, Video QA, and AVQA baselines; code released under open license.

problem: Unified, generalizable semantic control in video generation is challenging; existing methods enforce inappropriate pixel-wise priors, rely on non-generalizable finetuning, or require task-specific architectures.
approach: Video-As-Prompt reframes control as in-context generation using reference videos as semantic prompts, employing frozen Video DiT with Mixture-of-Transformers expert and temporally biased position embeddings for robust context retrieval.
contribution: Single unified model achieves 38.7% user preference rate rivaling commercial models; VAP-Data contains 100K paired videos across 100 conditions; strong zero-shot generalization to diverse applications.

problem: Modern VLMs struggle with compositional reasoning, decomposing and recombining concepts; neuro-symbolic approaches are constrained by crisp logic or predefined predicates.
approach: NePTune blends VLM perception with symbolic reasoning via differentiable Python programs that combine imperative control flow with soft logic operators, enabling reasoning over VLM-generated uncertainty in a training-free manner.
contribution: Significant improvement over base models on visual reasoning benchmarks; effective compositional generalization and adaptation in novel environments.

problem: Molecular dynamics simulations are computationally expensive; deep generative models for trajectory generation either generalize poorly across systems or fail to exploit structural information effectively.
approach: Pretrained Variational Bridge maps initial structures into noised latent space and transports toward stage-specific targets via bridge matching, unifying training on single-structure and paired trajectory data; RL optimization for protein-ligand holo states.
contribution: Faithfully reproduces thermodynamic and kinetic observables from MD while delivering stable, efficient generative dynamics for proteins and protein-ligand complexes.

problem: Graphon models for complex networks lack accurate parameter selection methods; tuning parameters that govern smoothness is critical but computationally expensive.
approach: Proposes a novel graphon cross-validation method for selecting tuning parameters and estimation approaches; asymptotically parallel to estimation error.
contribution: Cross-validation score is theoretically sound and computationally efficient; consistently delivers superior accuracy across simulations and real-world applications.

problem: Existing Table-Text QA benchmarks are small, manually curated, error-prone, and contain shallow questions rarely demanding multi-hop reasoning, aggregations, or complex operations.
approach: SPARTA automatically generates large-scale benchmarks by enriching tables with grounding tables from passages, synthesizing nested queries, ensuring executability via provenance-based refinement, and enforcing realistic structure.
contribution: End-to-end pipeline produces thousands of high-fidelity question-answer pairs covering aggregations, grouping, and deep multi-hop reasoning; state-of-the-art models show significant performance gaps.

problem: Classical scaling laws suggest more data improves performance, but recent methods achieve better results with smaller curated datasets; when and why less is more remains unclear.
approach: Theoretical framework modeling data curation with an imperfect oracle selecting examples by difficulty and correctness; derives exact scaling law curves revealing phase transitions for when curation improves generalization.
contribution: Provides analytical conditions and exact phase transition curves; validates on ImageNet that curated datasets can outperform full datasets and mitigate model collapse.

problem: Conformal prediction methods in long-tailed classification force binary choices between small prediction sets with poor class-conditional coverage or large sets that are impractical.
approach: Introduces prevalence-adjusted softmax for macro-coverage and label-weighted conformal prediction to smoothly trade off set size against class-conditional coverage.
contribution: Guarantees marginal coverage while achieving reasonable set sizes on long-tailed datasets like Pl@ntNet-300K and iNaturalist-2018 with 1,081 and 8,142 classes respectively.

problem: Modern MLLMs have undermined traditional text-recognition CAPTCHAs; current defenses remain vulnerable to AI advances in 2D image understanding.
approach: Spatial CAPTCHA leverages fundamental differences in spatial reasoning between humans and MLLMs, generating dynamic questions requiring geometric reasoning, perspective-taking, occlusion handling, and mental rotation via procedural generation.
contribution: Humans vastly outperform 10 state-of-the-art MLLMs; best model achieves only 31.0% Pass@1 accuracy, confirming effectiveness as both security mechanism and diagnostic tool.

problem: Achieving exact invariance to specific symmetries requires designing bespoke architectures for each symmetry group; scaling to 230 space groups in crystallography is impractical.
approach: Develops a single architecture using symmetry-adapted Fourier bases constructed via explicit constraints on Fourier coefficients; weight sharing enables models to leverage structural similarities and overcome data sparsity.
contribution: Single model automatically adapts weights to enforce invariance to any input space group; achieves competitive performance on material property prediction and zero-shot generalization to unseen groups.

problem: Self-consistency with majority voting for LLM reasoning leads to diminishing accuracy returns and high computational overhead; efficient confidence-guided filtering is needed.
approach: Deep Think with Confidence leverages model-internal confidence signals to dynamically filter low-quality reasoning traces during or after generation without additional training or hyperparameter tuning.
contribution: On AIME 2025, DeepConf@512 achieves up to 99.9% accuracy and reduces generated tokens by up to 84.7% compared to full parallel thinking; integrates seamlessly into serving frameworks.

problem: Medical QA benchmarks focus on multiple-choice or fact-based tasks; open-ended mental health answers that mix symptoms, treatment, and emotional needs require balance between clinical caution and sensitivity.
approach: CounselBench developed with 100 mental health professionals contains 2,000 expert evaluations across six clinical dimensions with span-level annotations; CounselBench-Adv includes 120 expert-authored adversarial questions.
contribution: Expert evaluation reveals LLMs achieve high scores on several dimensions but exhibit recurring issues including unconstructive feedback, overgeneralization, limited personalization, and safety risks like unauthorized medical advice.

problem: 2:4 semi-structured pruning offers hardware acceleration but existing methods incur substantial performance degradation in LLM deployment.
approach: ARMOR factorizes weight matrices into 2:4 sparse cores wrapped by low-overhead block diagonal matrices that act as error correctors; optimization via block coordinate descent with convergence guarantees.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art 2:4 pruning on Llama and Qwen models; generalizes to N:M patterns and unstructured sparsity while retaining inference speedups.

problem: Automated academic presentation generation lacks coherent narratives, insufficient aesthetic quality, and constrained self-adjustment; existing methods cannot effectively improve without reliable evaluation.
approach: EvoPresent framework unifies narratives, aesthetic-aware designs, and realistic delivery; PresAesth is a multi-task RL aesthetic model providing scoring, defect adjustment, and comparative feedback for iterative self-improvement.
contribution: EvoPresent Benchmark comprises 650 top-tier papers with multimodal resources and 2,000 slide pairs; findings show high-quality feedback is essential for effective agent self-correction.

problem: Cooperative perception requires sharing rich sensor information over limited communication bandwidth; existing selection strategies reduce features but bandwidth stress remains high.
approach: CooperTrim exploits temporal continuity to identify features capturing environment dynamics while avoiding redundant static information; conformal temporal uncertainty metrics guide adaptive bandwidth allocation.
contribution: Achieves up to 80.28% bandwidth reduction while maintaining comparable accuracy; improves IoU by up to 45.54% with 72% less bandwidth compared to other selection strategies.

problem: Existing distillation methods for generative models are framework-specific and data-free; incorporating real data requires complex adversarial training with discriminators.
approach: RealUID provides a unified distillation framework for all matching models (diffusion, flow, bridge matching, stochastic interpolants) that seamlessly incorporates real data supervision without GANs.
contribution: Unified theoretical foundation extends previous distillation methods and enables practical real-data-supervised training across different generative frameworks.

problem: Distribution mismatch between pre-collected offline preference data and evolving model policy limits alignment effectiveness; existing methods fail to adapt to model's dynamic learning state.
approach: MetaAPO couples data generation with training via a lightweight meta-learner that evaluates online sampling benefits and assigns sample-wise meta-weights balancing online and offline data quality.
contribution: Consistently outperforms preference optimization baselines on AlpacaEval 2, Arena-Hard, and MT-Bench while reducing online annotation costs by 42%.

problem: Brain-computer interfaces lack natural communication through oversimplified semantic representations and interpretability challenges in translating neural activity to meaningful language.
approach: Semantic Intent Decoding models meaning as compositional semantic units; BrainMosaic decodes multiple semantic units from EEG/SEEG via set matching and reconstructs sentences through semantic-guided reconstruction.
contribution: Enables interpretable and expressive BCI-mediated communication; demonstrates substantial advantages over existing frameworks on multilingual EEG and clinical SEEG datasets.

problem: DDIM inversion for diffusion models produces latent encodings with structural patterns lacking diversity; smooth image areas have less diverse noise predicted, limiting editability.
approach: Analyzes the relation between initial noise and generated samples; replaces first DDIM inversion steps with forward diffusion process to decorrelate latent encodings.
contribution: Enables higher quality image edits and interpolations by fixing latent diversity issues; shows prior methods do not fully resolve structural pattern problems.

problem: Autoencoding-based context compression for LLMs creates fundamental mismatch: models optimize for reconstruction diverging from downstream tasks, weakening useful features.
approach: Semantic-Anchor Compression directly selects anchor tokens from context and aggregates information into their KV representations via anchor embeddings and bidirectional attention modification.
contribution: Eliminates autoencoding training requirement; consistently outperforms existing compression methods on context compression tasks without training overhead.

problem: MoE-based LLMs require substantial memory for deployment despite computational efficiency; existing compression methods suffer significant accuracy drops even at modest compression rates.
approach: Mixture-of-Basis-Experts decomposes expert weight matrices via W=AB where A is expert-specific and B is a linear combination of shared basis matrices across MoE layer; learned by minimizing reconstruction error.
contribution: Reduces parameter counts of Qwen3-235BA22B-2507, DeepSeek-V3, and Kimi-K2-Instruct by 24-30% with only 1-2% accuracy drop (about 2% relative).

problem: GNN pooling relies only on last-layer features, potentially under-utilizing important intermediate activations; over-smoothing in deep networks exacerbates representation shift across layers.
approach: HistoGraph applies unified layer-wise attention over intermediate activations followed by node-wise attention to model node representation evolution across layers.
contribution: Consistent performance improvements on graph classification benchmarks; particularly strong robustness in deep GNNs by leveraging historical activations.

problem: Extending image-based latent diffusion priors to high-definition video restoration is challenging; frame-by-frame methods result in temporally inconsistent reconstructions.
approach: LVTINO leverages Video Consistency Models that distill video diffusion into fast generators capturing temporal causality; conditioning mechanism bypasses automatic differentiation for efficient restoration.
contribution: First zero-shot plug-and-play inverse solver for high-definition video restoration; achieves state-of-the-art quality with few evaluations while ensuring temporal smoothness.

problem: Existing logical reasoning benchmarks focus on canonical puzzles, risking memorization of solution patterns and masking deficiencies in novel rule application and strategy adaptation.
approach: HardcoreLogic introduces 5,000+ puzzles across 10 games with systematic transformations along three dimensions: Increased Complexity, Uncommon Elements, and Unsolvable Puzzles.
contribution: Reveals significant performance drops in Large Reasoning Models achieving top scores on existing benchmarks; exposes heavy reliance on memorized patterns and gaps in genuine reasoning.

problem: Long-horizon video prediction from observations and actions remains underexplored for general-purpose scenarios; existing world models lack precise action interaction capabilities.
approach: Astra uses autoregressive denoising with temporal causal attention for streaming outputs; noise-augmented history memory balances temporal coherence; action-aware adapter and mixture of action experts handle heterogeneous modalities.
contribution: Achieves interactive, consistent, general long-term video prediction; supports various action forms across autonomous driving, robot grasping, and camera control tasks.

problem: High-resolution 3D physics simulations require scalable neural surrogates that capture global context; existing architectures lack speed and accuracy for complex PDE dynamics.
approach: P3D combines CNN-Transformer backbone for 3D simulations; pretrains on small patches that fuse for global solutions guided by sequence-to-sequence models for long-range dependencies.
contribution: Outperforms baselines on 14 different PDE dynamics; scales to 512^3 isotropic turbulence; generates probabilistic samples of turbulent flows capturing underlying statistics.

problem: MLLMs lack deep emotional understanding despite progress; genuine affective intelligence requires explicit Theory of Mind modeling of mental states from which emotions arise.
approach: HitEmotion diagnoses emotional reasoning deficits across cognitive depth; ToM-guided reasoning tracks mental states and calibrates cross-modal evidence; TMPO uses intermediate states as process-level RL supervision.
contribution: Exposes deep emotional reasoning deficits in state-of-the-art models; ToM-guided reasoning and TMPO improve accuracy and yield more faithful, coherent rationales.

problem: Current video generation models are limited to short clips; long video generation requires temporal causality modeling and fine-grained temporal control absent from existing approaches.
approach: SteinsGate combines Temporal Action Binding for decomposing videos into scene descriptions and action sequences with Causal Video Continuation for autoregressive coherent narratives; uses Video Path Integral for action causality.
contribution: Generates natural, smooth multi-action long videos with accurate temporal control; converts pre-trained diffusion models into autoregressive continuation models.

problem: Graph positional encodings using message passing face theoretical limitations; capturing topological features for graph classification requires effective structural representations.
approach: LEAP combines differentiable approximation of Euler Characteristic Transform (DECT) and local variant to create trainable local structural positional encodings for graphs.
contribution: Unlocks topological feature extraction; evaluated on real-world datasets and synthetic tasks designed to test topological feature recovery.
